definition: A deque is a double-ended queue: elements can be added or removed at either end in constant time. It can act as a stack, a queue, or a window that slides from both sides. A circular buffer or a doubly linked list is the usual backing store.

complexity.time: Add and remove at either end are O(1).
complexity.space: O(n) space for the elements themselves.

examples: A sliding window that drops items from the front and adds at the back
An undo stack that can also peek at the oldest item
